attempted_claim: Let G be the Petersen graph, i.e. up to isomorphism the unique 3-regular girth-5 graph on 10 vertices and 15 edges (Kneser KG(5,2): vertices are 2-subsets of {1,2,3,4,5}, adjacent when disjoint). Let k be any field, R=k[x_v : v in V(G)], and I=I(G) the squarefree monomial edge ideal, with s-th symbolic power I^{(s)} defined as the intersection of the s-th powers of the minimal primes of I (equivalently via minimal vertex covers). Using combinatorial Rees-algebra data (Rees equations / cover-induced containments) together with Waldschmidt-constant estimation, determine the exact Waldschmidt constant \hat{\alpha}(I)=lim_{s\to\infty} \alpha(I^{(s)})/s and the exact resurgence \rho(I)=sup{m/r : I^{(m)} not subset I^r}, and on that basis decide whether the boundary containment I^{(3)} subset I^2 holds or fails, for all m,r>=1. A complete answer proves the exact values (or intervals tight enough to force the stated pair) and either gives a Rees/cover proof of I^{(3)} subset I^2 or exhibits an explicit monomial with certificates of membership in I^{(3)} and non-membership in I^2.
claim_type: exact Waldschmidt, resurgence and boundary containment decision
decisive_failure: No exact resurgence value is claimed: the lower bound rho >= 6/5 (alpha/hat-alpha and the C5 extremal family) has no matching general upper bound, so containment for arbitrary (m,r) is undecided; the I^(4)-level box checks (1890 minimal exponents, zero failures vs I^2 and I^3) cover only isolated pairs; originality of the partial certificates was not checked since literature search was prohibited in the recovery pass, so no emergent originality is asserted.
